A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same controller-generator research, renamed Matryoshka Pilot in v2. The complete 38-page and 46-page documents, including appendices, provide readable text, equations, tables and figures supporting comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments on LaMP, GSM8K/GSM-Hard and ALFWorld, including benchmark results, ablations and case studies.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds MATH500 evaluation, optimizer and controller variants, additional comparisons, and cost analyses.

M1.justification: The controller-generator and iterative DPO core remains, but v2 introduces an iterative SimPO training alternative (B.4). Its reasoning/planning inference specification adds controller re-decomposition after six unsuccessful generator refinements, followed by another execution attempt (F.4–F.5); v1 E.3–E.4 terminated after those refinements. These are substantive procedural extensions beyond renaming IGO to IDPO.

E1.justification: v2 adds the harder MATH500 reasoning benchmark (B.2, Figure 7). The five evaluated LaMP tasks, GSM8K/GSM-Hard and six ALFWorld task types remain, making this a focused extension within the existing reasoning domain.

E2.justification: New comparisons include Fermi and ORPO for LaMP, LEAP variants and Bbox-Adapter for GSM8K, black-box controllers for planning/reasoning, and self-consistency (B.3, B.6–B.7). B.3 explicitly imports published baseline scores rather than reporting reruns. Table 2 drops its separate PAG(gpt-3.5) row, while corresponding LaMP comparisons reappear in Table 15.

E3.justification: The reported inference procedure extends the previous six-reflection stopping rule with controller re-decomposition and further refinement. Added experiments vary MATH500 inner-loop iterations and one versus two outer loops, evaluate Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct instead of the original LLaMA-3-8B controller, and use eight-response majority voting for self-consistency. These introduce substantial evaluation designs; the PDFs do not establish that every retained result was rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds outer-loop feedback ablations on MATH500, SimPO-versus-IDPO tests, controller-backbone robustness tests, black-box-controller controls, and API-cost analyses (B.2–B.7). G.2 replaces the lemon-tree case with a two-turn pencil-problem example. The earlier profile-count, sample-efficiency and generator-refinement analyses remain, sometimes relocated.

E5.justification: Both versions retain seed 42 and point-estimate performance reporting. Dataset statistics containing ± values are unchanged. v2 introduces no repeated-run averaging, confidence intervals, error bars or significance-testing procedures.

E6.justification: Reported method scores change: LaMP-2N accuracy moves from 0.832 to 0.823 and LaMP-4 BLEU from 4.144 to 4.298 (Table 1); GSM8K/gpt-3.5 accuracy changes from 0.911 to 0.931 (Table 3); ALFWorld overall success changes from 95.52% to 96.27% (Table 4). Numerous MATH500, variant, comparator and cost results are added. Changed inference specifications prevent interpreting these revisions as clean same-setting gains. Section 4.2 still quotes obsolete LaMP accuracies.

T1.justification: v2 expands the mathematical treatment with a joint trajectory definition, autoregressive probability factorization and contrastive objective (Equations 1–3). It derives elimination of fixed generator terms from SFT and iterative DPO objectives (Equations 7 and 10–11), and supplies iterative SimPO objectives. This adds substantive definitions and derivations beyond v1's guidance-level DPO formulation.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain lightweight white-box control of black-box generators, environmental feedback, and iterative self-improvement. The introduction and conclusion retain the same headline improvements of 3.19%, 7.46% and 5.82%. Renaming and additional supporting experiments do not redefine these core claims.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly interprets DPO as a replaceable training choice, discusses controller-backbone flexibility, and attributes reduced API expenditure to guidance requiring fewer generator interactions (B.4–B.7). These extend the existing feedback-based explanation. The privacy and misuse limitations are largely retained in the reorganized impact appendix.

D1.justification: v2 adds per-dataset generation costs, token pricing, GPU usage and training durations (F.2), plus explicit controller re-planning prompts (H.1–H.2). It removes v1's conditional GPT-4o fallback description for LaMP and the statement that implementation code accompanies supplementary material and will be released on GitHub. The PDFs do not establish actual code availability.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations and positioning involving Fermi, ORPO, LEAP, SimPO and self-consistency, including distinctions from training-free prompt optimization (B.3). Several earlier citations disappear. The principal ICL/adapter/RL framing remains, and the SuperICL/HYDRA discussion is relocated to Appendix C. The abstract also removes the earlier suggestion that ICL requires accessible model parameters.

P1.justification: v2 shortens the abstract and conclusion, reorganizes the formulation and optimization exposition, and changes terminology throughout. Profile-count analysis, the small-model related-work discussion and ethics material move into appendices; the standalone reproducibility section and future-work paragraph disappear. Together these materially reorganize the narrative beyond adding experiments.

P2.justification: v2 adds numerous comparison, variant and cost tables plus MATH500 Figure 7; some added tables redisplay existing results. The profile-count plot moves from main-text Figure 5 to appendix Figure 6. Tables, captions, code listings and the conference layout are extensively reformatted, while the main framework diagrams remain substantially similar.

improvement.justification: New MATH500 tests, controller/optimizer controls and cost disclosures strengthen support for the existing framework. However, v2 retains obsolete LaMP accuracies in Section 4.2, reports different outputs for identical code in its replacement GSM-Hard example (G.2), and removes the code-access statement. These reporting weaknesses limit the net benefit to a modest improvement.
